title: Prehospital Antibiotics for Patients With Suspected Sepsis: The PITSTOP-Antibiotics Factorial Randomized Clinical Trial
summary: In this blinded Ontario factorial trial, 2,091 adults were randomized and 2,020 had primary mortality outcomes. Prehospital ceftriaxone produced 182/1009 deaths (18.0%) versus 186/1011 (18.4%) with placebo: RR 0.97 (95% CI 0.81–1.17). Administration-related adverse events occurred in 6.2% versus 1.5%, mainly injection-site pain.
comparator: IM saline placebo; subsequent hospital antibiotics permitted.
population: Adults with suspected infection, fever ≥38°C and SBP <100 mm Hg; four Ontario paramedic services.
limitations: Fever/hypotension selection and a single antibiotic/route limit generalization to other EMS systems and infections. Small mortality effects remain possible; pre-antibiotic cultures were not obtained.
intervention: Ceftriaxone 1 g IM in the ambulance, as studied.
whyItMatters: Adding 1 g IM ceftriaxone before hospital care did not improve survival. This challenges routine use of this specific prehospital regimen; it does not support delaying appropriate ED antibiotics.
evidenceNotes: Publisher methods, tables, harms and limitations reviewed; supplements unreviewed. Abstract/Table4 agree; prose contains an inconsistent placebo death count, so table/abstract used. Exact-DOI searches found no verified correction. Prior PHANTASi and current guidance address differing populations; existing guideline recommendations are not automatically superseded. SSC2026 conditionally suggests EMS antibiotics for definite/probable sepsis with hypotension and >60-minute anticipated evaluation delay, with very-low-certainty evidence; this trial tests one regimen, not every implementation. Official source reviewed: https://www.sccm.org/clinical-resources/guidelines/guidelines/surviving-sepsis-campaign-international-guidelines-for-management-of-sepsis-and-septic-shock-2026
primaryEndpoint: Death before hospital discharge, through day 90.
